overview: This item defines a first-class set of Jido effects for behavior tree execution, so that ticking, node status changes, and side-effectful actions are expressed declaratively rather than embedded in control flow. The goal is to design a small, composable effect vocabulary (e.g., tick node, schedule child, read/write blackboard, emit telemetry/logging) that can be reused across different behavior tree strategies. Effects should cleanly separate pure decision logic from IO, making behavior tree execution observable and testable. The work includes mapping core behavior tree concepts (selectors, sequences, decorators, leaf actions, abort/interrupt rules) into effect types and payload schemas, defining a behavior-tree-specific effect namespace, and common metadata (tree id, node id, tick id, correlation keys). The output is a stable effect API with typespecs, schemas, and examples.
title: Define effects for behavior tree execution
